title: The Eternity of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The eternity of God means that God has no beginning, no end, and is not ruled by time. He is the everlasting God who was, who is, and who is to come.
summary: The eternity of God means that God has no beginning, no end, and is not ruled by time. He is the everlasting God who was, who is, and who is to come.
christFocus: Jesus Christ shares the eternal glory of God and reveals the everlasting Lord to His people. Through Him, believers receive eternal life and hope that outlasts time, death, and decay.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is before all things. Mountains, nations, generations, and worlds have beginnings and endings, but God is from everlasting to everlasting. Time does not create, limit, age, or threaten Him.

God’s eternity means He sees and rules history differently than creatures do. Human life is brief and fragile, but God is not hurried, surprised, or diminished by the passing of days.

Scripture calls Him the eternal King and the everlasting God. He inhabits eternity and yet draws near to the humble and contrite. His transcendence does not make Him cold; His eternal life becomes a refuge for His people.

In Christ, eternal life is given to believers. The eternal God has entered human history through the Son so that mortal people may receive life that cannot be destroyed by death.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People are often ruled by time: fear of aging, regret over the past, anxiety over the future, and pressure over what feels delayed. The eternity of God lifts believers above panic and reminds them that their lives are held by the everlasting Lord.

This doctrine gives comfort when life feels short or unstable. The eternal God is the dwelling place of His people from generation to generation, and His promises are not weakened by time.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Number your days before the eternal God. Do not live as though this present moment is ultimate. Trust the One who is before you, behind you, above you, and with you in Christ. Let His eternity teach you patience, worship, hope, and faithfulness.
